Hi, I work at Meta Superintelligence Labs, and previously worked on knowledge graphs and search, automated reasoning and formal methods, type systems, and on computational biology/genetics/genomics. I have a PhD from MIT CSAIL, where my research focused on automated reasoning, especially string constraint solvers.

I’m interested in learning Lean and its applications, and in contributing to Mathlib. My PR adds two small lemmas about prime divisibility for natural-number factorial and binomial APIs: one characterizes when a prime divides an ascending factorial, and the other applies this to characterize when a prime p > n divides choose (k + n - 1) n in terms of divisibility of one of the consecutive factors k, k+1, ..., k+n-1. https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/39366

This looks like a helper to a Sylvester-Schur type result. While you wait for this PR to be approved, I suggest you work on a modification involving products of an irreducible arithmetic progression: \prod_{1<=i<=n} (k +i * d), where gcd(k,d)=1. This will be useful for the extended results by Sylvester and by Schur. [Disclaimer: my version has gcd(n,d)=1 and looks at \prod_{1<=i<=k} (n+ i * d) . ]
sender_full_name: J. J. Issai (project started by GRP)

content: Thank you. I have a few more lemmas in mind. Will wait a bit to submit them to incorporate learnings and guidance from this PR.
